Outdure Academy · current system · 17 August 2026

How Academy actually works today

Answers to Craig's twelve questions, checked against the deployed code and a read-only look at the live database. Screenshots are from the running academy; learner names and email addresses are masked.

Read this first

The platform is built and live, but the real training has not been rolled out. Both proper courses — Standard Training and Trained Installer Training — are still drafts, imported and video-attached on 14 August, waiting on quiz sign-off and publication. Everything that has happened on the system so far is pilot testing on three small early courses.

That changes one of the questions. There is no body of recurring learner or dealer problems yet, because there are barely any learners.

01

Training structure

Three levels, and no more: Course → Section → Lesson.

  • There is no programme or pathway above a course, and no module between section and lesson. A course is the unit someone enrols in, completes, and is certified for.
  • An assessment is not a separate object — a quiz is a lesson type, sitting in the running order like any other lesson.
  • Lesson types available: video, quiz, text, PDF. SCORM exists in the database schema but is not built.
  • Question types: multiple choice (one answer), multiple choice (many answers), true/false. No matching, ordering, free text or file upload.
02

Lesson completion

There is no settings screen for this. The rules are fixed in the platform — an author cannot change them per lesson or per course.

Video
The learner clicks “Complete & continue”. Manual.
Text
Same — manual button.
PDF
Same — manual button.
Quiz
Automatic on passing. No manual option.

Four consequences worth being explicit about, because they surprise people:

  • Watching the video is not required. The player records watch time and furthest position — that feeds Insights and lets someone resume across devices — but it does not gate the Complete button.
  • No sequential locking. Every lesson is a live link. A learner can jump to lesson 40 on day one. No prerequisites anywhere.
  • Course complete means 100% of lessons complete. When the last one ticks over: enrolment closed, tier advanced, certificate issued, certificate email sent.
  • Progress is append-only. A completion cannot be undone by anyone, and an admin cannot complete a lesson on a learner's behalf. The support “view as” mode is strictly read-only.
03

Assessments

A quiz has exactly two settings:

Pass threshold
Percentage. Defaults to 70.
Attempts allowed
Defaults to 10.

That is the entire settings surface. No time limit, no randomisation, no question pools, no option shuffling, no per-answer feedback, no proctoring.

  • Grading happens on the server at submit. Each question is all-or-nothing — a many-answer question needs exactly the right set. Score is the percentage of points earned.
  • After submitting the learner sees one line: “You scored 74%. Passed.” or “Not passed — try again.” They are never shown which questions they got wrong, and never see the correct answers.
  • Failing blocks nothing. Every other lesson stays open. But the quiz lesson stays incomplete, so the course cannot complete — no certificate, no tier advancement. That is the only lever a failed assessment pulls.
  • Attempts exhausted locks the learner out with “Ask your administrator to reset it.” There is no reset button in the admin. Today that message points at something that does not exist; it needs a database change. Nobody has hit it yet.
  • Every attempt is written to a tamper-evident log with the score, the pass/fail, the threshold at the time, and the attempt number — so the evidence survives someone later changing the pass mark.
04

Contractor training and Trained status

It is automatic, and that is the only way it happens.

Each course carries a setting, Confers tier on completion, whose options mirror the Connect user types: Contractor Registered → Trained → Verified → Strategic Partner, and Dealer Stockist → Reseller. On 100% completion the learner's tier advances to whatever the course confers. It only ever moves upward and within the same group — it never demotes, and a Dealer course cannot push a Contractor sideways.

Two things to be clear about:

  1. There is no manual control. No screen sets, overrides or removes a tier. If someone's tier is wrong, or they should be Trained without doing the course here, that is a database edit.
  2. It flows nowhere. The tier codes are a hand-maintained copy of Connect's user types. Academy and Connect are separate systems with separate databases and no connection between them — no sync, no API call, no shared table. Nothing on Outdure.com, in Connect, or in any directory learns that someone became Trained. Someone has to carry that across by hand.

Trained Installer Training is set to confer Trained. Three tier advancements have happened so far, all pilot.

05

Dealers and Product Champions

Not represented at all.

There is no organisation, company, branch, location or site anywhere in Academy. The model is flat: a person belongs to the academy with a role (Admin, Instructor, Learner) and optionally a tier tag. There is no way to record that someone works for a dealer, no parent and child between accounts, no Product Champion designation, and no way for one person to see or manage another's training.

The only dealer-shaped thing in the system is the two Dealer tier codes, Stockist and Reseller — and those sit on an individual, not an organisation. No course currently confers either.

Where they live today: nowhere purpose-built

Dealer companies exist as records in Connect, which the CRM was migrated to from HubSpot. But that is a company record, not a structure training can hang off: there is no dealer location, no Product Champion designation as a field, and no link of any kind to Academy. The relationship “this location's champion, and the contractors trained under them” has no home in any system today.

It will need to be added, and the likely anchor is the Outdure website — so the dealer record the public site already implies becomes the same record that training and the installer directory hang off.

Sharpens the point in section 04: Academy's tier codes are a hand-maintained copy of Connect's user types, and Connect now holds the dealer records too. The one system Academy has no connection to is the one holding everything it would need.

This has a knock-on for Verified below: the target of 3–5 Verified installers per location cannot be counted until an organisation exists for the count to hang off. “Per location” presumes a location.

06

Verified contractors

Half of it exists, and it is the half that does not matter.

Verified exists as a tier, and a course can be set to confer it — two of the pilot courses are. So “complete this course, become Verified” works mechanically.

What does not exist is any verification process: no evidence or photo submission, no inspection record, no application, no review queue, no approve or reject, no assessor sign-off, no expiry or re-verification. Nothing in Academy asks a human to make a judgement about a contractor. If Verified is meant to mean more than “watched the videos”, that process is currently outside the platform.

Who owns the decision

Andrea — Partnerships & Activation
Owns the Contractor Partnership Programme and all four tiers. The Verified decision is hers.
Craig — Commercial & Legal
Supports at strategic level only, through one-to-many activation such as webinars and events. Not the approver.
Curtis — Technical Escalation
Designed the platform flow and the tier sheet. Internal only; never distributor-facing.

The system currently bypasses that ownership

Live right now, and it contradicts the governance above: two published courses are set to confer Verified automatically on completion — Outdure Pedestal Systems and DeckPlanr – Selecting Surfaces. Anyone who finishes either is granted Verified by the platform, with no checklist, no photos, no inspection, and no involvement from Andrea.

No real contractor has been affected — the only account holding Verified is a test account. But the mechanism is switched on, and it should be turned off (uncheck “Confers tier on completion” on both courses) before the real courses are published.

How Curtis proposed it should work

Design intent from the tier sheet, not an operating process. None of this is built, and none of it runs today.

  • Verified sits at level 4, reached after “Outdure Comprehensive Training” at level 3.
  • Open to Contractor and Pro Contractor only — not DIY, Dealer or Distributor.
  • Three requirements, all three needed: Check List Approved · Photos · Inspected Installer.
  • Each requirement is paired with a commercial note: checklist ↔ “Qualifying Lead for Supply & Install”, photos ↔ “Price m²”, inspection ↔ “20m² × $ × =”. That reads as Outdure supplying the job — an inference from the sheet's layout, worth confirming with Curtis rather than treating as settled.
  • Rewards: a directory listing as a Verified installer, plus a rebate. Both depend on the approval being recorded somewhere a directory can read — the same missing system of record as section 05.
  • Target density: 3–5 Verified installers per location.

The manual register was designed in from the start

Curtis's flow issues the Trained Installer certificate “and added to google sheet”. The Google Sheet is not a workaround that grew around a gap — it was the intended record from day one. Academy issues the certificate; the sheet, alongside Connect, is the register.

07

Automated communications

Seven emails. All transactional, all fired by something a person just did. There is no scheduler in the system at all.

Welcome
A new academy is created.
You've been invited
An admin invites someone from the user list (Users → All Users).
Request accepted
An admin accepts a self-service join request.
Reset your password
A learner asks for a reset.
You're enrolled
A learner enrols in a course.
Certificate ready
A course is completed and a certificate issued.
Receipt
A Stripe payment. Configured, but not used for these courses.

What that means in practice, which is the bigger point:

  • No reminders, no nudges, no chasing. Nothing goes to someone who enrolled and stalled, has not logged in, failed a quiz, or whose training is going stale.
  • No admin notifications. When someone requests to join, nobody is emailed — an admin has to notice it on the user list.
  • No template editing. All seven are written into the code. “Email Templates” and “Mass Emails” appear in the menu as coming-soon.
08

Reports and integrations

Reports

One screen — Insights — plus the certificates list.

  • Eight headline numbers: enrolments, completions, completion rate, learners, active in 30 days, new enrolments in 30 days, quiz attempts, quiz pass rate.
  • Video engagement per lesson: viewers, total watched, average per viewer, furthest point reached. This is the strongest thing in the system — real played time, not “clicked complete”.
  • Where learners get stuck: the most-attempted questions with average time spent and how often they are answered wrong.

There are no exports. None. No CSV anywhere, no scheduled reports, no training matrix, no gradebook, no per-learner progress report, no course roster to hand to anyone. The only file you can produce is a certificate, printed from the browser. Training Matrix, Gradebook, Scheduled Reports and Activity Log all appear in the menu as placeholders.

A full tamper-evident log of every change is recorded in the database — but no screen reads it, so it is unreachable without a developer.

Integrations

Supabase
Login and database.
Bunny Stream
Video hosting and playback.
Resend
Sending the seven emails.
Stripe
Payments. Wired up, not used for Outdure courses.
Sentry & PostHog
Error tracking and usage analytics.

And nothing else. No connection to Outdure.com, no connection to Connect, no contractor directory, no marketing or email platform, no SSO, no public API, no outbound webhooks. Academy is an island. The only way data has ever moved in was a one-off import script — that is how the 103 lessons and 125 quiz questions were loaded on 14 August.

An Academy ↔ Connect integration needs to be built

Connect is the one that matters. Since the CRM migrated off HubSpot it holds the dealer companies, the contractor records, and the canonical user types that Academy's tier codes are a hand-copied mirror of. The single system Academy has no link to is the system holding everything it needs.

Everything Academy produces — Trained, Verified, certificates, completion dates — has to be re-keyed by hand into Connect and the Google Sheet today. That link is the piece of work this whole picture points at.

09

Roles and permissions

Four roles exist, fixed in code. Three can be assigned from the user list — in the menu it is Users → All Users, though the screen it opens is titled “People” (one screen, two names; a small naming inconsistency in the product itself):

Learner
Enrols, learns, earns certificates. The default.
Instructor
Assignable, but currently carries no permissions the learner role lacks.
Admin
Full control of this academy — courses, people, certificates, settings.
Platform admin
Cross-academy. Not assignable from the UI; it exists for the people who run the platform itself.

There is no permissions model beneath the role — no per-feature toggles, no groups, no scoping a person to one course. A role is all-or-nothing, and the list above cannot be added to without a code change.

10

What a learner actually sees

Included because it bears on the manual work below: there is no admin-side enrol. An admin can invite someone into the academy, but only the learner can put themselves on a course, from the catalogue.

What has to be done by hand today

Every item here is a gap in the software, not a preference:

  1. Anything dealer or Product Champion related — the concepts do not exist in Academy.
  2. The whole Verified process — Academy can flip the flag, but cannot run the assessment.
  3. Telling Connect, Outdure.com or anyone else that someone is now Trained — no sync.
  4. Any chasing or reminding — no scheduler, so every nudge is a manual email.
  5. Any report anyone asks for — no exports; it has to be built off the database.
  6. Resetting a learner who has used all their quiz attempts — the error tells them to ask an admin, and the admin has no button.
  7. Fixing a wrong tier — no manual override.
  8. Undoing a completion — progress is append-only by design.
  9. Enrolling someone into a course — there is no admin-side enrol. Learners enrol themselves from the catalogue; an admin can only invite them into the academy.
  10. Adding learners in bulk — invitations go one at a time.
  11. Producing a certificate PDF — browser print only.
  12. Keeping the accreditation register — the Google Sheet, which was the intended record from the start rather than a workaround.

Decisions this raises

Not questions about the software — questions the software has surfaced:

  1. Turn off automatic Verified before the real courses publish. Two published courses grant it today with no inspection and no approver. This is a two-click fix and the only item here that is urgent.
  2. Build the Academy ↔ Connect integration. Connect holds the dealer companies, the contractors and the canonical tiers; Academy holds the training evidence and issues the accreditations. Nothing joins them, so every Trained and every certificate is re-keyed by hand. This is the structural gap, not a nice-to-have.
  3. Decide where dealer organisations, locations and Product Champions live. Neither location nor Product Champion is a structured field in Connect today. Nothing in the programme can be counted per location until they exist somewhere — including Curtis's 3–5 Verified installers per location.
  4. Confirm the commercial reading of the Verified requirements with Curtis — whether checklist, photos and inspection really do pair with Outdure supplying the job, or whether that is a coincidence of the sheet's layout.

Still genuinely open, and not answerable from the system: what learners, contractors and dealers actually come back with. That sits in the support mailbox and needs an export.
